info.bio:
Ghost es una banda de hard rock/heavy metal formada en el año 2008 en Linköping, Suecia. En el año 2010 lanzaron su primer demo que contiene sencillo "Elizabeth"; posteriormente editaron su álbum debut "Opus Eponymous" el cual ha recibido críticas positivas y con éste se han dado a conocer en distintas partes del mundo.

scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Fundiendo los estilos psicodélicos que preferían la jam libre (acid-rock, space-rock, raga-rock), muchos grupos esculpen empresas sonoras épicas: Fuzzhead, Crawlspace, Pressurehed, Farflung, Fuxa, Gravitar (el Metal Machine Music de Lou Reed con ritmo), Pelt, Primordial Undermind, Escapade y, por encima de todos, Bardo Pond (Bufo Alvarius, Amanita) y Hash Jar Tempo. Texas recupera la supremacía de la locura psicodélica (Ed Hall, Cherubs, ST 37, Mike Gunn, Charalambides, Linus Pauling Quartet, la Vas Deferens Organization de Dallas); San Francisco, la psicodelia ruidosa de Mason Jones (Trance, Subarachnoid Space). En Nueva Zelanda, Roy Montgomery (Dadamah, Dissolve), Dean Roberts, Flies Inside The Sun; en Japón, Kousokuya, Mainliner, Musica Transonic, Acid Mothers Temple, Ghost.

podcast.title: Ghost (Sweden, 1996) – Papa Emeritus = Tobias Forge; Nameless Ghouls; Arena-Level Success Despite Satanic Imagery
podcast.body: Ghost came together in Sweden in 1996 and became a worldwide phenomenon filling arenas. The only named member is the frontman Papa Emeritus (stage name of Tobias Forge), who dresses like a Pope from hell and cycles through different character names (Cardinal Copia, Papa Emeritus IV). All other band members are called Nameless Ghouls, each representing an ancient element (fire, water, wind, earth, plus ether). Rumored past Ghouls have included Dave Grohl. The satanic imagery has caused problems in the US Bible Belt. Their sound is a blend of hard metal, arena rock, doom metal, psych, symphonic metal, and gothic rock. "Ghost is hard metal, metal, arena rock, do metal, psych, symphonic metal, gothic rock, and more."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: "Ghoul Writer" Song Credits
podcast.body: All songs released by Ghost are credited to a generic "ghoul writer" to maintain the band's anonymity regarding songwriting credits. "All songs are credited to a ghoul writer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Anonymity and Autograph Protocol
podcast.body: With a few exceptions, band members maintain complete anonymity. During autograph sessions, they do not sign their names but instead use stamps featuring their respective alchemic symbols. "With the exception of a couple of slips and revelations, everybody is completely anonymous. And while they will do autograph sessions, they don't sign their names. They each have a stamp with their respective alchemic symbol."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Lawsuit Revealing Tobias Forge's Identity
podcast.body: A lawsuit brought against Papa Emeritus by some of the ghouls resulted in the public revelation of a few names, through which it became known that Papa Emeritus is actually Tobias Forge. "There was once a lawsuit against Papa Emeritus by some of the ghouls, which resulted in a few names being made public. This is how we know that Papa Emeritus is actually a guy named Tobias Forge."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Papa Emeritus Character Iterations
podcast.body: The Papa Emeritus character has evolved through five iterations, each appearing as a demonic pope or cardinal who worships Satan rather than Christian deities. "Papa Emeritus character has gone through five iterations so far, each looking like some demonic version of a pope or a cardinal that worshiped Satan instead of anything resembling Christian deities."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Papa Emeritus and Nameless Ghouls Lineup
podcast.body: The band's lineup consists of a frontman, Papa Emeritus, and a group of "nameless ghouls" who wear virtually identical costumes and face masks. "Papa Emeritus is up front while all the nameless ghouls appear in pretty much identical costumes and face masks. In fact, the lineup is listed as Papa Emeritus IV and a group of nameless ghouls, one of whom may or may not have temporarily included deep role."

podcast.title: Satanic Imagery and Performances
podcast.body: The Swedish band Ghost is considered shocking due to their do-metal live performances and their satanic appearance and trappings, which upset some people. "Some may consider the Swedish band Ghost to be a shocking band. That stems mostly from their do-metal live performances, and some people are bent out of shape by their satanic appearance and trappings."

podcast.title: Swedish Metal Group, Formerly Ghost B.C.
podcast.body: Ghost is a Swedish metal group that was once known as Ghost B.C. in the United States to prevent confusion with other bands sharing the name. "There are a number of bands with that name, but in this case, I mean the Swedish metal group who were once referred to as Ghost BC in the US to keep them from getting confused with someone else."

podcast.title: Symbolism and Alchemy
podcast.body: Their image incorporates special symbols, vestments, and references to alchemy and ancient elements such as fire, water, wind, earth, and also "ether." "There are special symbols, investments, references to alchemy and the ancient elements of fire, water, wind and earth. Oh, and ether too, for some reason."

podcast.title: Worldwide Fanbase and Grammy Success
podcast.body: Ghost has a massive worldwide fanbase and has received four Grammy Awards, becoming a significant concert draw despite limited radio play. "Ghost has a massive worldwide fanbase and four Grammy Awards to their name. And while they don't get on the radio too much, they've become a giant concert draw."

xref.title: Coachella Hologram Performance (2012)
xref.body: In 2012, a virtual Tupac Shakur made a striking appearance at Coachella during a set by Dr. Dre and Snoop Dogg. Though marketed as a hologram, it was technically an advanced projection using Pepper's Ghost techniques, appearing "awfully lifelike" and marking a pivotal moment in the development of simulated live performances. "Then in 2012, a very dead two-pock Shakur showed up at Coachella during a set featuring Dr. Dre and Snoop Dog."

xref.title: AI Voice Cloning in "Heart on My Sleeve" (2023)
xref.body: A "fake" version of Drake's voice was used in a fake duet with The Weeknd, created by an individual named Ghostwriter and posted in April 2023. This AI-generated track, titled "Heart on My Sleeve," was two minutes long and immediately sparked intense ethical and legal debates about the use of artists' voices without their consent. "The one that got everybody's attention was a fake duet between a fake Drake and a fake the weekend created and posted in April 2023 by someone named Ghost Rider."

xref.title: "Grey Ghost" Van
xref.body: In their early touring days, The Black Keys used a 1994 Chrysler van, which they affectionately named "The Grey Ghost," to travel between gigs. A similar old Chrysler van later featured prominently on the album cover of *El Camino*. "they were just scraping by and chugging from gig to gig in a 1994 Chrysler van that they called the Grey Ghost..."

xref.title: Avoidance of Second Floor
xref.body: Following her unsettling ghost encounter during a performance at the historic building (formerly the Bank of Montreal), harpist Joanne Jordan developed a strong reluctance to visit the second floor alone. Whenever she had subsequent engagements to play her harp at the venue, she made sure she was never by herself when needing to go upstairs, citing the area as "too spooky." "she made sure to never go up to the second floor by herself because she said that it's just too spooky up there."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Genre Fluidity and Influences
xref.body: Her music has shifted across many styles, including pop, rock, dream pop, psych, trip pop, and trap. Listeners can discern the "ghost" of iconic vocalists like Nina Simone, Frank Sinatra, Billie Holiday, and various torch singers in her sound. "If you close your eyes, you can hear the ghost of Nina Simone, Frank Sinatra, Billie Holiday, and any number of torch singers."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Ghost Encounter During Performance
xref.body: Toronto musician and harpist Joanne Jordan experienced a terrifying encounter while performing at an event in the former Bank of Montreal building, several years before it transitioned into the Hockey Hall of Fame in 1993. While playing her harp and admiring the Great Hall's dome and magnificent stained glass, she spotted a woman (later identified as the ghost of Dorothy May Elliott) standing by the second-floor railing, staring down at her. Jordan was shocked and recounted this vivid experience to the Toronto Star, learning about the building's permanent spectral resident only after her sighting. "I remember it so vividly because it's one of those things you'll never forget."

xref.body: Del the Funky Homosapien contributed as a rapper to the Gorillaz's debut album and was featured on the single "Clint Eastwood." xref.title: Impact of Bowie's "Coming Out"
xref.body: Boy George of Culture Club openly stated that his life was profoundly changed by David Bowie's public comments in January 1972 about being gay. Bowie's statement gave him the courage to embrace and be true to his own identity. "Boy George of Culture Club and Holly Johnson of Frankie Ghost of Hollywood say that their lives were changed by Bowie's comments."

xref.title: Mayonnaise Commercial Offer
xref.body: Early in their career, a UK-based mayonnaise manufacturer offered The Black Keys 200,000 pounds for the use of one of their songs in a TV commercial. Despite struggling financially and touring in their 1994 Chrysler van known as "The Grey Ghost," the band declined the offer, believing it would harm their artistic integrity, a decision that infuriated their parents. "The manufacturer of a brand of mayonnaise based on the UK offered the keys 200,000 pounds for the use of one of their songs."

xref.title: Producer of "Old Town Road" Beat
xref.body: Young Kio, a Dutch record producer, created the beat for Lil Nas X's "Old Town Road" by manipulating a sample from Nine Inch Nails' instrumental track "34 Ghosts 4" and selling it for $30 on his online store, where Lil Nas X purchased it. His real name is Kioa Rokima. "He stumbled upon a track called 34 Ghosts 4, an instrumental from the 2008 Nine-H Nails album Ghost 1-4."

xref.title: Professional Recording and Worsening Health
xref.body: By 1988, Daniel Johnston was well-regarded enough to record professionally in New York, but concurrently, his mental health deteriorated significantly. A notable incident involved him becoming convinced that "Casper, the friendly ghost," had stolen a plane key during a flight with his pilot father, leading to a crash landing and his subsequent commitment. "By 1988, he was well regarded enough to be given a shot of recording professionally in New York. At the same time though, his mental health got worse."

"they turned it down because they figured that would damage the credit."
